logline: Nearly a century after a nuclear apocalypse, one hundred juvenile delinquents are sent from their orbiting space station to test whether a ravaged Earth is survivable - and discover a world far more complicated than their leaders admitted.

renewal.note: The 100 concluded its seven-season, 100-episode run on September 30, 2020 on The CW. Creator Jason Rothenberg confirmed no continuation.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 holds 76% on Rotten Tomatoes from 37 critics - above average for The CW - with reviewers praising its premise and world-building energy while noting the rough genre-TV execution of its early episodes.

pull_quotes.text: A better-than-average CW sci-fi drama that splits its story into two halves.

seasons.review_body: The 100 debuted on The CW in March 2014 as a YA dystopian adaptation of Kass Morgan's novel series, arriving in the wake of The Hunger Games and Divergent. The first 13 episodes establish two parallel survival stories - the 100 teenagers on a decimated Earth navigating hostile Grounders, and the adult leadership on the Ark in orbit making impossible resource decisions. Variety's Brian Lowry noted it was 'better-than-average CW sci-fi' while finding the dual structure uneven. The 76% Rotten Tomatoes score from 37 critics reflects honest appreciation for a show finding its feet. The premiere season's most lasting accomplishment is establishing the show's moral universe: no faction is clean, survival demands compromise, and the teenagers become more dangerous than their wardens expected.

episode_reviews.title: Pilot
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot drops the 100 juvenile delinquents onto Earth without ceremony. The show earns its premise fast - the Earth is beautiful and lethal in equal measure - and establishes Clarke Griffin as a lead who will carry the series' moral weight.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The pod doors open and the 100 see Earth for the first time - a beat of genuine wonder the show earns by not overselling it.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 holds 100% on Rotten Tomatoes and is widely considered the show's creative peak, expanding the world to Mount Weather and forcing moral choices of genuine weight on its characters.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 is where The 100 became something no one expected from a CW genre show. The Mount Weather arc introduced a hidden society of survivors who had outlived the radiation by never leaving their bunker - and whose survival depends on harvesting the blood of the Grounders. The moral calculus is merciless and the show commits to its consequences. The 100% Rotten Tomatoes score reflects a critical consensus that the season elevated the series beyond its YA origins. Clarke's decisions in the finale became the season's defining conversation - the kind of morally unresolved ending that marks a show operating above its network tier. Season 2 remains the entry point recommended to sceptics of the series.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 replaces the Grounder-survival premise with a genuinely alarming moral puzzle at Mount Weather, upgrading the show from above-average genre TV to prestige-adjacent drama.

episode_reviews.title: Blood Must Have Blood, Part Two
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 2 finale delivers on every moral debt the season accumulated. Clarke's decision at Mount Weather is the moment The 100 permanently separated itself from comfort-zone YA storytelling and committed to genuine dramatic stakes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The finale's closing act - a decision with no clean resolution that the show never fully lets Clarke recover from across the remaining run.

bollymeter.basis: 83% on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics divided on an ambitious A.I. subplot that expanded the lore at the cost of some of Season 2's emotional intimacy.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 introduces the City of Light - a digital afterlife controlled by an AI called A.L.I.E. - alongside escalating political conflict between the surviving Grounder clans. The 83% critical score reflects a season that maintained the show's moral ambition but struggled with a bloated 16-episode count. A key death in episode 7 became a significant cultural flashpoint in discussions of queer representation in fantasy TV, generating sustained press coverage. The season's mythology-building ultimately pays off across the remaining run, though the payoff requires patience with an uneven middle stretch.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 broadens the canvas into A.I. mythology and faction politics, gaining world-building depth while losing some of Season 2's concentrated moral intensity.

bollymeter.basis: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes, with a second nuclear apocalypse threat focusing the narrative into a lean 13-episode sprint that critics found the tightest season since Season 2.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 faces the Praimfaya - a second wave of nuclear fallout that will render Earth uninhabitable again - and uses the existential deadline to restore the show's focus. The 13-episode count is the tightest since Season 1 and the narrative benefits from it. Characters are forced into impossible resource decisions that recall Season 2's best moral dilemmas, and the finale's time-jump gambit reset the show's geography in ways that genuinely surprised critics. The 93% critical score reflects a strong rebound from Season 3's mixed reception.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 4 tightens back to 13 episodes and regains the moral urgency of Season 2 by placing every character's survival under a hard countdown.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, with the six-year time jump and new prisoner antagonists energising the ensemble in ways critics found comparable to the show's Season 2 peak.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 opens with the survivors separated across space, the bunker and Earth's last valley of habitable land - a structural split that the show uses to reunite characters in genuinely changed circumstances. The prisoner ship arc introduces a credible antagonist in Charmaine Diyoza, and the 100% critical score reflects a season that satisfied the most demanding segment of the show's audience. The finale's second time-jump (130 years forward) demonstrated the series' continued willingness to remake its own premise rather than rest on established dynamics.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 5 rewards long-term viewers with the consequences of Season 4's time-jump, fracturing the ensemble across new survival contexts before a final-act reunion.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, with a new planet setting and a body-possession arc that critics found ambitious and frequently unsettling.

seasons.review_body: Season 6 moves the entire story to a new planet, Sanctum, and introduces the Primes - a ruling class who achieve immortality through mind-wiping and body possession. The conceit placed Eliza Taylor in a dual-performance challenge that received prominent attention in entertainment coverage as some of her strongest work on the series. The 100% critical score reflects a season that successfully delivered a reset without losing the show's thematic through-lines about power, survival and the cost of preservation. The mythology is dense after the Season 5 time-jump, rewarding the show's most committed long-term viewers.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 6 transplants the entire ensemble to an alien world and introduces a new form of moral horror - the Primes' immortality-through-erasure - that extends the series' core ethical arguments into new territory.

bollymeter.basis: 100% critical score but widely criticised by fans as a divisive final season, with the Transcendence finale among the most debated series endings in recent genre TV.

seasons.review_body: The seventh and final season of The 100 concluded on September 30, 2020 with a 100-episode run total, a milestone the show reached exactly as the title promised. The season introduces the Anomaly Stone mythology and time-travel elements that the critical consensus treated generously, but audience reception was sharply divided. The series finale's Transcendence concept - a metaphysical resolution to the show's long war over survival and power - satisfied some viewers as thematically consistent and infuriated others as a dodge of the show's materialist stakes. Despite the contested ending, the series as a whole stands as one of the more morally serious dystopian dramas the CW produced, outgrowing its YA origins most visibly in Seasons 2 and 4.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 7 reaches the 100-episode finish line with ambitious mythology but a contested finale that divided even the show's loyal audience.
